newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-Rural demand drives India M&M net higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rural demand drives India M&M net higher.

text.p: Leading Indian tractor and utility vehicles maker Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) said on Tuesday strong growth in rural disposable incomes drove its net profit 24.5 percent higher in the year ended March 31.
M&M said its net rose to 2.09 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), from 1.68 billion in the previous year. Income climbed to 36.07 billion rupees, from 28.99 billion in 1995/96.

"Increased volumes have come mainly from rural and semi-urban markets which have consistently been our key thrust areas," managing director Anand Mahindra said in a statment announcing the improved results.

Indian agriculture is estimated to have grown at around 3.7 percent in 1996/97, according to latest government data. The sector performed poorly in the previous year, with agricultural production recording a 0.1 percent fall.
M&M said tractor sales increased by 15 percent to 57,379 units in 1996/97, from 50,005. Sales of utility vehicles and trucks climbed 18 percent to 75,048 units from 63,583.

"Volume growth and price increases in utility vehicles during the year drove revenues. The results were mostly in line with expectations," said analyst Kapil Krishan at securities firm Peregrine Capital India.

Increased provisions for agricultural credit in rural areas, announced in the last two federal budgets, and good monsoon rains resulting in higher incomes for agriculture have boosted sales of vehicles in rural areas, analysts said.
"Tractor financing has increased and the coming monsoons are also likely to be good," said Niraj Somaiya, automobile analyst at securities firm HG Asia.
"The company should see a strong earnings growth of over 20 percent in the next two years," he said.

M&M's results came in slightly above the expectations of automobile analysts who had forecast a net profit of around 2.03 billion rupees. They said improved operating margins had driven profits above the consensus forecast.
M&M said in its results statement increased operating efficiency had boosted its performance.

"Besides increased sales of the company's vehicles and tractors, measures taken by the management such as stricter control over operations, higher productivity, better use of resources and efforts to reduce costs have all contributed to this improved performance," the firm said.
